tools.name: recommend_apps
tools.description: Ranks the apps in the AppFinder directory against a plain-language request and explains each pick with cited facts (what fits, what's missing, which apps a must-have rules out), plus one follow-up question that would narrow the list.

tools.name: search_apps
tools.description: Full-text search of the directory by name, keyword or job (most relevant first).

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: One app's listing: description, categories, pricing, platforms, features, integrations, rating, its facts with sources, and published user reviews (count, average, reviews page; the latest excerpts once it has 3 or more).

tools.name: compare_apps
tools.description: Side by side: pricing, and the features, integrations and platforms both apps have or only one has.

tools.name: find_alternatives
tools.description: Apps that do what an app does (same category, most shared features first), and what buyers who wanted to replace it chose.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: The directory's categories with how many apps each lists.

tools.name: category_demand
tools.description: The public demand report of a category: the share of buyers who asked the advisor for each feature, integration, security need and budget in the last 90 days (anonymous totals), and how many listed apps answer each.

tools.name: check_listing
tools.description: Whether a website already has a published AppFinder listing, and its page. Call this before list_my_app.

tools.name: list_my_app
tools.description: Use this when a maker wants to list their own app, product or open-source project on AppFinder, get it discovered, launch it, or find a free backlink for it: listing is free (no votes or fee), and while the maker shows the AppFinder badge on their site, the listing links to the app's own website wit

tools.name: prepare_listing
tools.description: Same as list_my_app, kept for older clients: prefer list_my_app. Fills in AppFinder's submission form and returns a private link for the maker to review and submit.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "list_my_app" is 849 chars, far longer than this server's median (143). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

evidence.snippet: Use this when a maker wants to list their own app, product or open-source project on AppFinder, get it discovered, launch it, or find a free backlink for it: li…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_app, list_my_app · Private data: list_my_app, prepare_listing · Public sink: category_demand, list_my_app, prepare_listing.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_app, list_my_app · Private data: list_my_app, prepare_listing · Public sink: category_demand, list_my_app, prepare_listing

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_app" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "One app's listing: description, categories, pricing, platforms, features, integrations, rating and its facts with sources." → after: "One app's listing: description, categories, pricing, platforms, features, integrations, rating, its facts with sources, and published user reviews (count, average, reviews page; the latest excerpts once it has 3 or more)."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
